matches.rationale: Finding 2 directly challenges the same asserted representation of the multimodal update as a single matrix \(\Delta W\) in \(h=W_0x+\Delta Wx\). It explains that the modality-specific and attention-based terms cannot constitute such a linear matrix update, identifying the core invalidity of the decomposition.

No finding identifies the stated misuse of \(\sqrt{N_t}\) instead of an embedding-dimensional scaling factor. The findings discuss shape errors and a possible \(d\)-versus-\(r\) inconsistency, which are distinct from the ground-truth \(N_t\) normalizer defect.
No finding discusses the text-token cross-modal zero term or whether it is written as \(B\mathbf{0}_{N_t}\) rather than \(\mathbf{0}_{N_t}\).

pred_verdicts.rationale: It identifies a plausible matrix-shape incompatibility in the cross-attention product, but not any listed ground-truth defect.
It correctly detects that the claimed single linear update matrix \(\Delta W\) is incompatible with the modality-dependent and nonlinear update construction.
It raises a separate potential \(d\)-versus-\(r\) normalization and notation conflict rather than the listed \(N_t\)-scaling defect.
